“What is wrong? Why do you hesitate? The Holy Grail is offered in exchange. I should think the terms overwhelmingly favorable.”

The priest is right.

There is no reason for her to hesitate here.

And yet—

*I believe the path I followed—the person I have been until now—was not a mistake.*

She cannot drive those words from her mind.

That was the heart that loved her country—the heart of an ordinary girl before she became king.

But it was not the heart she possessed as king.

The king she became could believe in only one thing: the self who had reigned.

To deny that self would be to deny the many things she had taken from others.

—What was lost cannot be restored.

Writhing in agony, her Master continued to insist upon that truth.

Yes. It is wrong.

She was raised as king and lived as king.

There had been no mistake in that.

Then—if destruction was the result, why had she been unable to accept it?

If she truly possessed no regret,

if she could take pride in the life she led, then she must not seek to live it again.

Shirou's lament echoes within her breast.

The tears would disappear.

The pain would disappear.

Even the cruel weight that gouged into his heart would disappear.

It would be forgiveness beyond compare: salvation of the self through erasure.

But—

if everything were made never to have happened, where would all the feelings stolen from others go?

Enduring the pain and grieving for them is itself the repose she can offer what was lost.

Therefore, if she desires to begin again, she must begin not in the past, but now.

If there is something she left undone,

she cannot return to the past and repeat it. She must begin at this moment to build the dream she failed to realize.

He casts us an amused glance, snaps his fingers, and summons the final actor onto the stage.

Saber's voice rises, seething with hatred.

…Questions she has carried for years.

It is as though she is calling him to account for the tragedy of ten years ago.

pages.en:
“Naturally. I have no intention of killing Saber. She belongs to me.

“But if the Holy Grail is to be summoned, I cannot simply let matters end there.

“For the ritual to be completed, one more Servant must die.”
